lead: `session.py --wrap` cannot commit a rename: a `## commit:` naming the path that went away is refused with "no such path", and naming only the new one leaves the deletion uncommitted.
body: Every named path is checked against the disk before a byte is written, and the commit it makes is pathspec-limited, so no spelling of the section carries a `git mv` — and `git add -- <old>` would exit 128 anyway once the index has the rename. Commit a renaming slice yourself, `git add -A -- <dir>` then `git commit -F`, after `nv verify` is green, and leave the wrap the docs.
